claims.statement: The navigation fragment describes opening the dashboard from the upper-left GitHub logo and switching from the username dropdown to a desired organization. Its screenshot caption shows linked organizations but was not visually inspected. Navigation is not membership verification, role authority, complete organization inventory, or an actual context switch.
The feed note describes a new feed as public preview subject to change at the pin. It supplies no stable behavior contract, current availability, feature definition, or verified feed content.

The tab note describes an unspecified new tab as public preview subject to change. The filename suggests a For you feed, but isolated text alone does not define the tab's algorithm, eligibility, or completeness; no current lifecycle claim is made.

The home-dashboard note describes an updated home dashboard as public preview subject to change at the pin. It is not a verified deployed interface, current release status, or stable project-accounting source.

The recent-activity fragment lists open issue/PR selection triggers: opening one, comments on one's opened item, reopening one's item, review requests, assignments, commit references, and one's comments. These personalized qualifying events do not establish exhaustive repository activity, all open tasks, reviewed/accepted work, complete chronology, or issue closure; no private activity was collected.
